headline: Nov 4-17: Dhaka to host 15th SAFF Championship
summary: The premier international football tournament for South Asia returns to Bangladesh for the first time since 2018.
details: Dhaka will host the 15th SAFF Championship from November 4 to 17, as confirmed by the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) in a press release on Sunday.
This marks the first time the region's premier international football tournament returns to Bangladesh since 2018, with all member associations expected to participate.
The official logo for the championship will be unveiled in Dhaka on July 25, followed by the tournament draw in Thimphu, Bhutan, on August 1.
SAFF General Secretary Purushottam Kattel expressed delight over the venue and dates, noting the tournament's special place in the hearts of South Asian football fans.
Kattel highlighted that Bangladesh's role as host is particularly exciting given the rapidly growing interest in football across the country.
caption:
Football returns to the capital! Dhaka is set to host the 15th SAFF Championship this November.

Dhaka will host the 15th SAFF Championship from November 4 to 17, as confirmed by the South Asian Football Federation (SAFF) in a press release on Sunday.

This marks the first time the region's premier international football tournament returns to Bangladesh since 2018, with all member associations expected to participate.

The official logo for the championship will be unveiled in Dhaka on July 25, followed by the tournament draw in Thimphu, Bhutan, on August 1.

SAFF General Secretary Purushottam Kattel expressed delight over the venue and dates, noting the tournament's special place in the hearts of South Asian football fans.

Kattel highlighted that Bangladesh's role as host is particularly exciting given the rapidly growing interest in football across the country.

headline: Accused in 32 cases re-arrested after escaping court lock-up
summary: Md Samrat Mondol slipped out of his handcuffs and fled the Gazipur Metropolitan Police Court lock-up before being caught by Rab within 24 hours.
details: The Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has re-arrested Md Samrat Mondol, 28, an accused in 32 criminal cases, less than 24 hours after he escaped from the Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Court police lock-up.
The suspect escaped yesterday around 2:00 PM by slipping one hand out of his handcuffs and fleeing the premises while lined up at the reception desk.
Following the escape, Gazipur Sadar Police Station filed a case under Section 224 of the Penal Code against the suspect.
Rab-1 and Rab-14 conducted a joint operation in the Kashar area of Mymensingh Kotwali Police Station early today to capture him.

caption:
He slipped out of his handcuffs and vanished from a court lock-up. Now, he's back in custody.

The Rapid Action Battalion (Rab) has re-arrested Md Samrat Mondol, 28, an accused in 32 criminal cases, less than 24 hours after he escaped from the Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Court police lock-up.

The suspect escaped yesterday around 2:00 PM by slipping one hand out of his handcuffs and fleeing the premises while lined up at the reception desk.

Following the escape, Gazipur Sadar Police Station filed a case under Section 224 of the Penal Code against the suspect.

Rab-1 and Rab-14 conducted a joint operation in the Kashar area of Mymensingh Kotwali Police Station early today to capture him.

Samrat Mondol was originally arrested on July 19 from a rented building in Khunia Madhyapara, Gazipur, during an operation where three others were also detained.

After the latest arrest, the suspect has been handed over to Gazipur Sadar Police Station for further interrogation and legal proceedings.
